part_title: Medical Speech, Clinical Entities and Safe Review
review_basis: Visually inspected all 29 original public/course-visuals/aif-course/module-08 numbered WebP images individually in order. Narration rewritten following exact diagram arrows, visible text/examples, numeric values, callouts, and exam comparisons, with product lifecycle caveats.

scenes.title: Amazon Transcribe Medical
scenes.narration: The two input modes at top left are live medical dictation and prerecorded clinical audio. Both can feed Amazon Transcribe Medical, which performs speech-to-text recognition using medical vocabulary. The example output reads Patient reports knee pain. The next green panel requires clinician review and correction before a final clinical note is stored in an electronic health record or another system. The lower-left worked example repeats the clinician's spoken phrase and the resulting transcript. The middle comparison separates Transcribe Medical, which starts from speech, from Comprehend Medical, which starts from existing text and extracts clinical entities. The right privacy panel calls for least-privilege IAM, encryption, data retention limits and suitable network controls. An AWS service being HIPAA-eligible is not a blanket compliance guarantee. A transcription error or extracted word must be checked before making any medical decision.

scenes.title: Amazon Comprehend Medical
scenes.narration: Read the example clinical note on the left: Patient reports knee pain; ibuprofen prescribed. The upper analysis branch enters Comprehend Medical DetectEntitiesV2, which returns illustrative clinical categories including a condition mention knee pain and medication ibuprofen. A clinician reviews those mentions in context; they are not an independent diagnosis or treatment instruction. The lower branch enters DetectPHI, which searches for possible protected health information. This operation identifies candidate sensitive text but does not automatically remove or mask it. The application must enforce its privacy policy and validate any de-identification before sharing. The bottom exam summary gives the service-selection decision: use DetectEntitiesV2 for clinical entities, DetectPHI for possible identifying information, and Transcribe Medical first only if the original input is audio. Keep permission boundaries and professional clinical interpretation outside the extraction model.

scenes.title: Medical transcription and entity extraction workflow
scenes.narration: This slide compares two complete medical information routes. Along the top, a clinician dictates Patient reports knee pain. The audio goes into Amazon Transcribe Medical, becomes written transcript text, and then enters Comprehend Medical. The illustrated output identifies a medical-condition mention, an anatomy term knee and a sign or symptom pain. A clinician verifies the result. Along the lower route the clinician already has a typed note, so there is no reason to transcribe audio: the text goes straight into Comprehend Medical. The two worked examples below reinforce those same alternatives. The yellow exam panel adds DetectPHI as a separate optional operation. It can identify possible protected information, but it does not sanitize text for you. The sample knee-pain sentence contains no identifying information in the example. These output labels are illustrative; never equate them with confirmed diagnoses or promised API responses.
